children: Bamboo Insurance Services unveiled terms of a planned initial public offering that could give the insurance distribution platform an initial market capitalization topping $3 billion.

Bamboo on Monday said its two largest investors, buyout firm CVC Capital Partners and White Mountains Insurance Group, plan to sell 35 million Bamboo shares at between $18 and $20 each in the offering.

Assuming the underwriters exercise an option to buy an additional 5.25 million shares, CVC will still own 69% of Bamboo's Class A common shares after the IPO, while White Mountains will own about 14%.
Bamboo, based in Midvale, Utah, isn't selling any shares in the IPO and won't receive any proceeds from the offering.
Bamboo said it would have about 156.3 million shares outstanding after the IPO, for an initial market capitalization of around $3.13 billion at the $20-a-share high end of the expected price range.
White Mountains late last year sold a controlling stake in Bamboo to CVC in a deal that valued the platform at $1.75 billion.
Bamboo said it has applied to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol BMB.
